findings.title: Zero/negative flusher_processes silently disables flushing
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.__init__ num_processes is min(max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) with max_processes = max_processes or len(...). A value of 0 falls back to len() silently, a negative value is truthy so num_processes becomes negative, range(negative) is empty and no processes are created. With empty assigned_shards num_processes is also 0. In all these cases submit() still accepts messages and advances drift but no background process ever calls flush_segments(), so segments sit in Redis forever with no error. Validate max_processes >=1 and assigned_shards non-empty or fall back to 1 process.

findings.title: Flusher restart leaks old worker and double-flushes shards
findings.body: In _ensure_processes_alive the old worker is replaced via _create_process_for_shards() immediately after process.kill() without join()/close(). For the threading.Thread test path the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard is false so nothing stops the old thread at all. The old worker keeps looping on the same shards while the new worker starts, so two workers call buffer.flush_segments()/done_flush_segments() and produce() for the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces and racing Redis deletes. Kill must be followed by join/close and threads must be stopped before replacement.

findings.title: join() abandons remaining flusher processes on timeout
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.join() the loop computes remaining_time and does break when the deadline expires. Breaking exits the for loop entirely, so any processes not yet waited on are never joined nor terminated and join() returns while workers are still alive. The single-process predecessor always waited then terminated its worker. The loop should continue to terminate remaining workers or record that shutdown timed out, not silently leave them running.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards
findings.body: SpanFlusher.main emits spans.buffer.flusher.produce with tags={"shard": shard_tag} on line 185 but spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce with tags={"shards": shard_tag} on line 199. Dashboards and alerts grouping by shard will miss half the timers. Use the same tag key in both timers.

findings.title: Multi-process flusher test never flushes
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit creates 4 partitions with flusher_processes=2, asserts process counts and shard totals, then joins without submitting any spans, advancing drift, or checking output, backpressure, or per-process shard assignment. It cannot catch duplicate production, lost shards, or the restart/join bugs introduced by sharding. Extend it to write spans on multiple shards and verify each segment is produced exactly once.
